Autophagic dysregulation is central to the pathogenesis of dry AMD, where impaired clearance leads to lipofuscin accumulation, oxidative stress, and subsequent RPE degeneration. Disruption in autophagic flux is linked to the accumulation of damaged proteins and organelles, fueling chronic inflammation and cellular demise, all of which are evident in AMD pathology (kaarniranta2023autophagyinagerelated pages 2-3, liton2023autophagyinthe pages 23-24).
